title: Goals filed with the federal housing department, and what was reported back
question: What did the Mayor's housing office tell the federal government its grants and local money would achieve over five years, and what did it report?
finding: The 2020 to 2025 plan filed with the federal housing department carries 106 numbered indicators under 29 goals. By the City's own final report, 59 (56%) reached the five-year goal and 8 ended below half of it. The plan expected $4.01 billion across those goals and reports $4.09 billion spent. The furthest short among indicators with a goal in at least three years: # of housing-office affordable housing tenants at risk of eviction that receive notification of eviction support services (126 against a five-year goal of 4,812).
how: The goals table at the front of the housing office's report to the federal housing department for 2024-25 (the last year of the five-year plan) was read from the report's text: for each indicator the five-year goal, each year's goal and each year's reported result. Reported results for the five years are added up and set against the five-year goal. The money columns are the plan's expected and reported spending for the whole goal that the indicator sits under, from all sources.
limits: These figures are compiled by the housing office from what its grantees report and are not checked by an outside body; the federal department receives them but does not audit each count. The report does not break results down by provider. Five-year goals were set in early 2020, before the pandemic, and housing completions depend on construction schedules, so a low share can reflect delay rather than failure. The table is read from a text layout and a figure can fall in the wrong column; check the report page before relying on a single row. Some indicators are counts that cannot sensibly be added across years, which overstates the share reached.
